newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh to set up national stock exchange.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh to set up national stock exchange.

text.p: Bangladesh will set up a national stock exchange (NSE) and a central depository system (CDS) in an attempt to stop manipulation in the country's capital market, Bangladesh Finance Minister S.A.M.S. Kibria said.
The NSE will be fully automated and equipped with modern technology and infrastructure, he told parliament on Wednesday night.
"The NSE will be devoid of all sorts of conflicts and ensure full transparency and accountability...," he said.
On Monday, a cabinet meeting chaired by Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina approved the proposed NSE.
The country currently has two stock exchanges -- Dhaka and Chittagong.
Stock market players have blamed manipulation and malpractice for sharp fluctuations in the Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE) benchmark index since late last year.
Brisk trading by thousands of retail investors began around mid-1996 following a period of relative political stability and fresh investment incentives for foreign and local investors.
The DSE benchmark index jumped to the 3,600 level by October from less than 1,000 last June in frenzied trading. The market, however, has suffered a long run of bearishness since November.
On Wednesday, the DSE index closed at 1,803.31.
In November, the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), alarmed by rising share prices, set a price fluctuation limit of five percent on shares from the previous day's level.
In the same month, the central bank ordered commercial banks to stop offering credit to investors against share certificates, sparking the market's slide.
SEC officials said the setting up of the NSE would expand and restructure the country's capital market.
The minister said Bangladesh was negotiating with "some donor agencies to set up a central depository system with a view to stop forgery and malpractice in share transfers.
He said the government had formed a surveillance team to investigate alleged share market manipulation and irregularities.
